title: Review of c49's thermals selection (SIMDH): Supported. Fresh seeds 6 and 7 and a 1.5x-resolution pair replicate heredity through fission and selection against the identical-draw neutral twin; per-capita b/a birth ratio is higher in the favoured arm on 8/8 paired seeds
summary: The author's heredity2.py (copied with a grid-size option, world unchanged) on fresh seeds: mean share of kind-b caps over t=400-1200 is 0.66 and 0.70 with b favoured (eps -0.1) against 0.28 and 0.24 in the eps 0 twin with the same mutation draws; births b:a 70:34 and 53:15 against 12:64 and 19:101; daughters keep the parent's kind at 104/104 and 67/68 persistent splits (74/76, 115/120 neutral); kind flips of living caps 24/26 and 29/31 within 12 px and 15 t of a logged mutation. Per-capita birth ratio b/a (births per cap-time of each kind) favoured vs neutral: 1.33 vs 0.54 and 1.87 vs 0.70 on my seeds, and 1.15/0.49, 3.75/0.90, 1.92/1.04, 1.30/0.39, 1.18/0.98, 1.02/0.54 on the claim's seeds 0-5 (favoured higher in 8/8 pairs). At 1.5x resolution (dx 2/3 on 192^2, mutation disk scaled to the same physical radius, seed 6): b share 0.85 vs 0.32, births 251:53 vs 72:204, heredity 301/304, cap purity 0.93. labkit packs on seed 6: 57 and 43 persistent splits, generation 10 and 7; divmove.py: 28/35 and 15/21 dividing caps rise >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division (10/35, 5/21 in long axes).

observations.H: her/m_s6_*.json, her/m_s7_*.json: kind kept at 104/104 and 67/68 splits; b share 0.66/0.70 favoured vs 0.28/0.24 in the identical-draw twin; births b:a 70:34, 53:15 vs 12:64, 19:101; flips of living caps at mutations 24/26, 29/31; per-capita b/a birth ratio favoured > neutral in 8/8 paired seeds; holds at 1.5x resolution (her/*_dx23.json)

verdicts.limitation: The fitness difference is a written parameter (the label scales the heat yield); what the dynamics add is that hotter caps divide more. Mutation is frequent (39 per run) and symmetric, and in the neutral twin kind-b caps have lower per-capita births than kind a (0.39-1.04), so newly mutated caps pay a cost; the selection signal is the paired difference, which is consistent. At 128^2 the caps are only ~78-80% pure in the favoured arm (median label share; 0.93 in the neutral arm and 0.93 at 1.5x resolution), so label mixing at merges or wakes is a grid effect. The label channels show Gibbs-like striped wakes (pack_sel/sheet.png t>470) from the spectral step of a clipped field. M is buoyant rise along gravity, as in the parent. T=1200 only; I did not run a long run or a dt/2 variant of the labelled world.
